title: Wizard generate step intermittently unreliable
description: Mitigated by the Tailwind CSS migration: the wizard's document generation now authors Tailwind classes inline during structure generation instead of a separate CSS-rules-writing phase, and the second AI call only sets styles.variables (brand palette) instead of a full CSS-rules object - much shorter total output, lower truncation/omission risk. Verified: the editor-transform happy-path test (which hits the real configured AI_PROVIDER, not a mock) went from failing on live model runs before the prompt rewrite to 4/4 passes after. Residual variance remains possible if the live model picks Tailwind syntax outside the allowlist's scope (e.g. arbitrary-value shadow colors) - that surfaces as a normal invalid_operations rejection, same as any other allowlist miss, not a truncation failure.

CSS_PROPERTY_ALLOWLIST and styles.rules validation remain fully functional and tested for backward compatibility with pre-migration documents, so this item is no longer open-ended for new content. The equivalent ongoing-maintenance item going forward is Tailwind class allowlist coverage, tracked implicitly via apps/ai_assistant/tailwind_classes.py.

Explicitly completed before a third consumer because the shared API is isolated and covered by a Node regression.

title: Image upload for the wizard

Registered in state.assets, but never AI-authored: wizard_service.py builds assets server-side from exactly what the client already uploaded, and the model only picks a URL from that list to put in . document_validation.py validates the shape regardless (check_asset_entry, url must be under /media/). Minimal wizard UI (file input + thumbnail strip) wired into the existing question-form step.

title: styles.rules gained @media support
description: editor-core.js's buildCss() already rendered styles.mediaQueries (dead code, never populated) and it was completely unvalidated on the Python side - a latent CSS-injection gap. Fixed both at once: document_validation.py now validates styles.mediaQueries (allowlisted query string via check_css_media_query, nested rules reuse the same selector/declarations checks); the wizard styles prompt now tells the AI it can use it. Scope: only covers wizard full-document generation, not the editor's incremental AI-transform.

title: Structured request logging/metrics for AI usage and error rates

Bonus: the wizard views had the same uncaught-exception gap as the transform 500 fix - added the same except Exception catch-all there too.

title: Autosave projects

Added the same revision-retention cap (20) to apps/projects/views.py that UserTemplate already has.

title: Tailwind CSS migration
description: Styling moved from a custom JSON DSL (styles.rules: AI/editor-authored {selector, declarations} objects validated against CSS_PROPERTY_ALLOWLIST) to Tailwind utility classes on attributes.class, validated against a finite allowlist (tailwind_classes.py: is_allowed_tailwind_class/check_class_list, wired into operations.py's set_attribute and sanitize.py's check_attributes). New Tailwind v4 CLI build pipeline (pnpm run build:css): a management command materializes the class allowlist into a safelist sentinel file that is Tailwind's ONLY content source (tailwind-input.css uses source(none) plus explicit @source), since AI-chosen classes never appear in any file Tailwind could otherwise scan, and because Tailwind's default whole-project auto-scan was verified to compile any Tailwind-shaped string found anywhere (including test fixtures). Wizard document generation now authors classes inline during structure generation; the second AI call only sets the brand-color palette. The editor's per-element quick-style panel now toggles Tailwind classes instead of writing an inline style="" attribute (a second, previously undocumented styling mechanism this consolidated away). styles.rules/mediaQueries/keyframes remain in the schema and keep rendering for backward compatibility with every pre-migration Template/UserTemplate/Project row - verified end-to-end with a hand-seeded legacy document (still renders its old CSS, its gallery thumbnail, and remains editable). Docker/CI/local setup updated to build the CSS (Node 20 required - Debian bookworm's apt nodejs is too old for Tailwind v4).

title: Public template publishing + storefront (products, Stripe checkout, digital downloads)
description: UserTemplate gains is_published/public_slug (stable once set); new GET /t/<slug>/ (PublicTemplateView) renders a full standalone document server-side (apps/editor/rendering.py's public_page_html) for anonymous visitors, no editor scripts, 404 identically for nonexistent and unpublished. New apps/storefront app: Product (price_cents, optional image, optional digital_file for downloadables, validated by real magic-byte sniffing not extension/Content-Type) and Order (the permanent purchase record, created ONLY by a signature-verified Stripe webhook, never the checkout-redirect view). PaymentProvider abstraction (FakePaymentProvider/StripePaymentProvider) mirrors the existing AIProvider/FakeAIProvider swappable pattern - PAYMENT_PROVIDER defaults to fake, tests never touch the real Stripe API. Checkout always re-reads price from the DB, never trusts the client. Digital downloads are served through a token-gated view (never a static /media/ URL) with a download-count cap; the success page explicitly handles the webhook-vs-redirect race condition via a direct provider session lookup fallback instead of assuming the Order already exists. Editor UI: Publicar/Despublicar toggle in the save modal, a Productos management page (/productos/), and an Insertar producto control that adds a real product card with a working Comprar form to the page. Verified end-to-end with real Playwright runs: publish+view+unpublish, create a product with an image and PDF (owner-scoped), insert a product card, and the full anonymous checkout -> pending -> simulated webhook -> paid flow. Real Stripe test-mode keys were not available in this environment - the full real-Stripe-hosted-checkout-page round trip was not run; only the FakePaymentProvider path was verified live.

title: Fix AI-rejected max-w-4xl class and enable YouTube/Vimeo iframe embeds
description: A user-reported screenshot of the AI panel rejecting an instruction ("agrega este video de YouTube") with a generic "cambios no válidos" error had two independent real causes, both found via live server-log reproduction rather than guessing from the screenshot. (1) tailwind_classes.py's max-w utility family only allowed the numeric SIZING_SCALE, missing Tailwind's separate named container-width scale (max-w-4xl, prose, none, etc.) - added MAX_WIDTH_NAMED_SCALE, scoped to max-w only (w/min-w/h/min-h/max-h unaffected). (2) iframe was fully forbidden in sanitize.py's FORBIDDEN_TAGS, silently blocking a legitimate, common request - replaced with a tag-specific src-prefix allowlist (youtube.com/embed, youtube-nocookie.com/embed, player.vimeo.com/video) so arbitrary iframe src is still rejected (clickjacking/phishing risk on now-public template pages) but real video embeds work. AI system prompt updated to convert watch URLs to embed URLs and use aspect-video instead of an arbitrary pb-[56.25%] hack. Verified end-to-end by re-running the exact original failing instruction against a live server and confirming a successful add_node operation with a working iframe.

title: "Contenido rápido" presets (Hero/Beneficios/Texto/Imagen/Llamado/Footer) reference CSS classes that don't exist anywhere
description: Replaced the six legacy semantic preset class sets with finite, allowlisted Tailwind utility classes; added a regression for Hero, Image, and CTA preview rendering. Also fixed the stale removed structure-tab target that hid all panels after the first insertion.

title: Route ""Insertar producto"" through the AI instead of a hardcoded unstyled node
description: Superseded by remove-storefront-payments: the storefront app (Product/PaymentGatewayConfig), the "Insertar producto" AI-card feature, EditorContext.available_products/available_gateways, the SYSTEM_PROMPT buy-card block, and the sanitize.py/operations.py data-product-id/data-buy-form digit-string special case have all been removed - sellers now paste their own purchase URL via the editor CTA prompt instead. Kept here for history only. Original: productCardNode() built a product card with zero Tailwind classes (h3/p/img/form/button, no styling at all). Rather than hand-writing Tailwind classes into the deterministic template, routed the insert through the existing AI transform pipeline: EditorTransformView now populates EditorContext.available_products server-side from the requesting user's OWN active products (id/name/price_cents/image_url) - never client-supplied, so the model can't reference a product it doesn't own or invent an id. The SYSTEM_PROMPT gained an exact card-shape spec (data-product-id/data-buy-form/action) the model fills with real Tailwind classes. editor-ai.js exposes a new EditorAI.requestInstruction(text) entry point (opens the drawer, forces global_mode, sends the instruction) that editor-core.js's insertProductButton now calls instead of pushing a hardcoded node. User explicitly chose this over a quick deterministic-Tailwind fix after being shown the tradeoff (latency/cost/variability vs instant/free/consistent).

title: Fix CSRF 403 on checkout/webhook for logged-in sessions
description: CheckoutView and StripeWebhookView are @csrf_exempt + AllowAny, but DRF's default SessionAuthentication runs its own CSRF check independent of that decorator whenever it successfully authenticates a request via session cookie - a logged-in visitor (e.g. the template owner testing their own Comprar button, as reported via screenshot showing 'CSRF Failed: CSRF token missing.' on /comprar/6/) got a 403 despite the view being explicitly csrf_exempt. Fixed with authentication_classes = [] on both views (no reason to authenticate a fully public/AllowAny request at all). Existing tests never caught this because the api/anon_api fixtures use force_authenticate, which bypasses DRF's real auth+CSRF pipeline entirely - added a regression test using a real client.login() session with enforce_csrf_checks=True, verified it 403s without the fix and 302s with it.

title: Fix fake-provider checkout stuck forever on Procesando tu pago
description: With PAYMENT_PROVIDER=fake (default, no Stripe keys configured), FakePaymentProvider marked a session paid instantly but nothing ever created the Order row - that only happens in StripeWebhookView.post, and there is no real Stripe server in dev/test to ever deliver that webhook. Reproduced live: a real logged-in browser session got permanently stuck on 'Procesando tu pago... Todavia estamos confirmando tu pago' right after the checkout CSRF fix (row 46) unblocked the redirect itself. Fixed by extracting the webhook's order-creation logic into a shared _record_order_for_session() and having CheckoutView call it directly right after session creation, ONLY when the provider is FakePaymentProvider - real Stripe checkouts are untouched, still require the actual signed webhook.

title: UI/UX: consolidate 3 drifted design-token sets into one shared stylesheet
description: Extracted the canonical palette, typography, radius, and shadow variables into static/shared/tokens.css, linked it across server-rendered surfaces, and verified it structurally and in a real browser.

title: Multi-gateway checkout (Stripe/Mercado Pago/PayPal/Braintree/Wompi/PayU/ePayco/Bold)
description: Executed per PAYMENTS.md (deleted after this close-out - see openspec/specs/storefront/spec.md for the permanent behavioral contract, CHANGELOG.md for the shipped-feature record). Buyer picks gateway at checkout; PaymentGatewayConfig is owner-scoped and Fernet-encrypted at rest (apps/storefront/crypto.py); each gateway has real+Fake* provider pair behind GATEWAY_REGISTRY (apps/storefront/payments.py); Order gained a gateway field, uniqueness scoped per (gateway, gateway_session_id); GatewayWebhookView tries every enabled seller's credentials for a gateway until one verifies the signature. New /config/ page + /api/payment-gateway-configs/ (credentials write-only, never returned). AI product-card prompt now emits one buy-form per available_gateways entry. Verified end-to-end via a real browser click-through: /config toggle -> publish page -> click real Comprar button -> gracias page, for the Stripe fake-provider path. Confidence/verification depth varies sharply by gateway (see openspec/specs/storefront/spec.md and learnings.jsonl id 2026-07-23-15): Stripe/Mercado Pago/Wompi/PayU/ePayco have local HMAC/checksum signature tests (accept+reject); PayPal/Braintree tested with mocked network/SDK calls; Bold's real webhook spec was never confirmable (JS-rendered docs returned no usable content) so BoldPaymentProvider.parse_webhook_event always raises rather than pretend to verify something unconfirmed - do not treat Bold as production-ready without first getting its real docs.

title: Fix legacy /comprar/<id>/ (no gateway) 404 on already-published pages
description: The multi-gateway checkout migration (row 49) changed /comprar/<id>/ to /comprar/<id>/<gateway>/, but a UserTemplate's buy-form action is a literal value baked into stored state JSON at insert time - never regenerated when the URL pattern changes. An already-published page's Comprar button 404'd for real (reproduced live via screenshot: /comprar/6/). Fixed with a legacy URL (checkout-legacy, same CheckoutView, gateway=None) falling back to the seller's first enabled PaymentGatewayConfig (deterministic order) - still 404s if the seller has enabled nothing at all via /config.

title: Deliver product for free (tracked $0 Order) when seller has no gateway enabled
description: Explicit user decision: rather than 404 (or an untracked silent giveaway) when a seller has zero PaymentGatewayConfig rows enabled, CheckoutView now delivers the product/downloadable directly AND creates a real, permanent Order (gateway=Order.Gateway.NONE, amount_cents=0, status=PAID) - auditable exactly like any real purchase. SuccessView accepts gateway=none. Verified end-to-end via a real browser click on a published page's Comprar button with no gateway configured at all.

title: Close CSS-value style-tag breakout gap (PROPOSAL.md item 4)
description: check_css_declaration/check_css_variable only rejected expression()/javascript:/@import/unsafe url() in a CSS value, not angle brackets or braces - a crafted value (e.g. red; } then a literal closing style tag then a script tag) would break out of the server-rendered inline style block in apps/editor/rendering.py (published pages), since that HTML is built via raw string interpolation, not DOM textContent. Found via a from-scratch review of corebunch/instatic's three-tier CSS sanitizer split. Fixed by extending CSS_VALUE_FORBIDDEN to also reject < > { } in both check_css_declaration and check_css_variable (same single choke point both operations.py's set_css_declaration/set_style_variable and document_validation.py's wizard full-document validation already route through).

title: Add architecture-as-tests suite (PROPOSAL.md item 5)
description: tests/test_architecture.py encodes three invariants from openspec/project.md's gotchas as CI-run pytest checks instead of only convention: no inline <script> with executable JS in any template (CSP script-src 'self' silently blocks it), no AI provider secret env-var name referenced in any static/**/*.js file, and editor-core.js's window.EditorCore facade stays appended near the end of the file rather than spliced into the original IIFE body. Writing the first check surfaced a real live bug: templates/storefront/payu_redirect.html had an inline <script> auto-submitting the PayU form after 250ms - silently CSP-blocked, so the auto-redirect never fired (the manual Continuar button still worked, so it was degraded, not fully broken). Fixed by moving it to static/storefront/payu-redirect.js and loading it with <script src>.

title: Add owner-scoped audit log for AI and template edits (PROPOSAL.md item 10)
description: New AuditEvent model (apps/editor, migration 0009) records ai_transform, ai_wizard_generate, template_create, and template_save actions with owner, target_type/target_id, and a small metadata blob (instruction text, operation count, template name) - closes a real debugging gap where the only trail of which AI instruction produced a given UserTemplateRevision was server.log, not queryable per template. Read-only GET /api/audit-events/, owner-scoped. palette_apply was dropped from the original proposal's action set since applying a palette preset is purely client-side (editor-core.js, no server round-trip to hook a write into); revision_restore was folded into template_save since restoring already goes through the same PATCH perform_update path. Surfaced as an Actividad panel in the save modal next to the existing Historial revision list.

title: Add upload placeholder color for saved images (PROPOSAL.md item 11)
description: UploadedAsset gained placeholder_color (image_processing.py's _dominant_color_hex, a one-pixel Pillow downsample, no new dependency), shown as a CSS background-color behind the thumbnail while the real file loads in the wizard's upload strip (template-wizard.js) and the editor's saved-image picker (editor-core.js). Substituted for a literal blurhash decode as originally proposed: a full blurhash needs a JS DCT decoder and static/editor/*.js has no build step to vendor one into, while a one-pixel average color gets the same don't-show-a-blank-box outcome with a one-line client-side style instead. Folders and per-page usage tracking (the other half of the original proposal item) stay deferred, no current pain point reported for a flat per-owner asset list.

title: Add HTML paste import (PROPOSAL.md item 12)
description: New apps/ai_assistant/html_import.py (html_to_node, stdlib html.parser only) converts pasted external markup into a node tree, routed through the exact same sanitize_node gate as AI-authored operations - zero new trust boundary. Simplified from the original proposal: class and style attributes are dropped outright rather than partially preserved through the Tailwind allowlist, since per-class mapping was materially more complexity than the feature warranted; the response's skipped_attributes count tells the client how many were dropped so it can say so instead of silently changing the paste. New POST /api/ai/editor/import-html/ (html_import throttle scope, 20/m, synchronous, no SSE/provider call), a Pegar HTML button and modal in the editor topbar, static/editor/html-import.js.

title: Add Ctrl/Cmd+K command palette to the editor (PROPOSAL.md item 13)
description: New static/editor/command-palette.js, entirely self-built DOM overlay (no template markup needed) with a filtered command list, dispatching by clicking the matching existing button rather than duplicating any logic. Scoped down from the original proposal: dispatches only to the always-available topbar actions (Guardar/Deshacer/Rehacer/Pegar HTML/Importar JSON/Descargar JSON/Copiar JSON), not the quick-insert content presets, which live inside modal-dependent state that would need its own investigation first. Verified live in a real browser (official Playwright container, host was missing Chromium system libs) via the new tests/e2e/command_palette.spec.js: open/filter/Escape and running a command from the palette.

Added a short paragraph after the existing wizard request-flow section for POST /api/ai/editor/import-html/ and GET /api/audit-events/, matching the doc's existing narrative style rather than a bare list.

title: Add AuditEvent per-owner retention cap (PLAN.md step 2; REVIEW.md gap)
description: AuditEvent grew unbounded with no purge path, unlike UserTemplateRevision (REVISION_RETENTION_LIMIT) and apps/analytics's purge_analytics command - flagged in REVIEW.md as a real inconsistency, since metadata stores AI instruction text indefinitely. Fixed with Option A from PLAN.md: a new AuditEvent.record() classmethod creates the row then prunes that owner's events to RETENTION_LIMIT=100 (self-enforcing, no scheduling dependency, same inline-prune shape UserTemplateRevision already uses). All three write sites (UserTemplateViewSet.perform_create/perform_update, EditorTransformView, WizardGenerateView) switched from AuditEvent.objects.create to AuditEvent.record. The read API's defensive slice now references AuditEvent.RETENTION_LIMIT instead of a separate duplicated constant.

title: Map a safe subset of imported inline styles to Tailwind classes (PLAN.md step 3)
description: HTML import (PROPOSAL.md item 12) originally dropped class and style entirely - REVIEW.md flagged this as understating the real UX cost, since pasting any styled snippet produced completely unstyled output. Added STYLE_TO_TAILWIND, a small (10-entry) allowlisted table of exact (property, value) matches (text-align, font-weight, font-style, text-decoration) mapped to their Tailwind class, each still re-validated through is_allowed_tailwind_class before being kept - never a general CSS-to-Tailwind converter, only known exact matches. Raw class= is still always dropped. skipped_attributes now counts only what's actually still dropped after mapping, not every style declaration. Updated the in-UI help copy and toast message to describe the new partial-mapping behavior instead of a blanket 'no se conservan'.

title: Widen command palette to quick-insert presets after investigation (PLAN.md step 4)
description: PROPOSAL.md item 13 originally scoped the command palette to topbar-only actions, since the quick-insert presets ([data-preset]) live inside #sectionModal and REVIEW.md flagged not having investigated whether they need the modal open. Investigated (read-only trace through editor-core.js): the preset click handler only reads button.dataset.preset, mutates state, and toggles CSS classes on already-existing DOM elements (setActiveTab) - nothing requires the modal to be visually open, and .click() fires the listener regardless of visibility. Widened command-palette.js's COMMANDS registry with the 6 presets (Hero/Beneficios/Texto/Imagen/Llamado/Footer) dispatched by CSS selector instead of id, generalizing run() to support both. Verified live (official Playwright container): inserting Hero from the palette with the section modal closed the whole time renders the same styled section as the existing modal-driven flow.

title: Fix htmlImportModal never opening, and switch EditorModals to a dynamic modal registry (round 2 PLAN.md step 1; found while fixing a REVIEW.md gap)
description: REVIEW.md round 2 flagged that command-palette.js never joined the shared EditorModals system (no Tab-trap, no focus-restore), unlike every other editor dialog. Wiring it in surfaced a real, separate, previously-undetected bug via live verification: editor-ai.js's EditorModals kept a hand-maintained array of exactly 5 modal element ids, and htmlImportModal (PROPOSAL.md item 12) was never added to it - clicking Pegar HTML silently did nothing, since EditorModals.open() only ever toggled visibility for elements literally in that list. No existing test (pytest or the full 17-spec e2e suite) had ever opened that modal through the UI; only its backend endpoint was tested. Fixed the root cause, not just the missing entry: modalElements is now built by querying every element matching the shared panel-modal dialog class/role once at load (closes this bug class for any future template-defined modal), plus a new EditorModals.register() for modals built dynamically in JS after that query already ran (used by the command palette). command-palette.js now calls EditorModals.open()/closeAll() instead of its own hand-rolled show/hide, gaining Tab-trapping and focus-restore-to-trigger for free. Verified live: Pegar HTML opens correctly, Escape restores focus to the triggering element, Tab stays trapped inside the open palette across 15 presses.

title: Add permanent e2e coverage for elementModal and paymentLinkModal opening (round 3 PLAN.md step 1)
description: REVIEW.md round 3 reviewed row 81's shared-modal-registry refactor and found the two most-used interactive surfaces in the editor - elementModal (the element inspector, opened via the floating action bar's Editar button) and paymentLinkModal (the double-click link/product flow) - had zero e2e coverage despite depending on the exact infrastructure just rewritten. Confirmed no regression via live verification first (both open correctly), then promoted that verification into permanent tests instead of discarding it. Selecting a floating-action-bar button by visible text failed during verification since makeActionButton renders icon-only text content (the label lives in aria-label/title, not textContent) - a real thing to know for anyone else writing a test against #vjpb-actions, not a product bug.

title: Add permanent e2e coverage for imagePickerModal opening; close the modal-coverage sweep (round 4 PLAN.md step 1)
description: REVIEW.md round 4 found row 82's coverage fix was incomplete, not wrong: it covered 2 of the 6 modalElements entries (whichever the previous round happened to think of), missing imagePickerModal (opened by double-clicking an img preview node), which depends on the exact same round-2 shared-registry refactor. Verified live first (insert an image via quick-insert, close sectionModal first since it visually overlaps the preview and intercepts the double-click otherwise, then double-click the image - modal opens correctly, no regression), then promoted to a permanent test. All 6 modalElements entries (elementModal, sectionModal, paymentLinkModal, imagePickerModal, saveTemplateModal, htmlImportModal) now have e2e coverage that they open - documented in REVIEW.md so a future round doesn't need to re-derive the list from scratch.

title: Fix run-local.sh and setup.sh hanging non-interactively on pnpm install; seed placeholder_color in mockup_data
description: Auditing the .sh scripts for currency: run-local.sh hung/aborted (ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY) when run without a TTY (an agent, a cron job) because pnpm install --frozen-lockfile prompts interactively to confirm recreating node_modules whenever its state doesn't match the lockfile - reproduced live, confirmed CI=true (which real GitHub Actions runners already set, masking this for actual CI) resolves it. setup.sh had the identical call and the same latent bug. Fixed both by prefixing with CI=true. Also found mockup_data.py's _create_asset never set the new placeholder_color field (added in this session's PROPOSAL.md item 11), leaving seeded UploadedAsset rows with an empty placeholder instead of demonstrating the feature - fixed by reusing the already-available colors[0] hex value. All four .sh scripts verified live end-to-end after the fixes: run-local.sh (server responds, migrations applied), stop-local.sh (actually stops the process it started), mockup.sh (flush+reseed succeeds, seeded assets now carry a real placeholder_color).

title: Add per-IP login rate limiting (PROPOSAL.md gap-analysis item 4)
description: Gap analysis found every API endpoint uses ScopedRateThrottle except the session-based /login/ form itself - no throttle reference anywhere in apps/accounts/views.py or config/settings/base.py. Added a small custom throttle on LoginView (Django's cache framework, no new dependency - django-axes was considered but rejected per ponytail, the cache framework already does per-IP counting well enough for a brute-force speed bump, not a hard security boundary needing Redis-backed cross-worker consistency): 5 failed attempts per IP within 5 minutes returns 429, counter resets on successful login. Verified live via real curl POSTs against a running dev server - 6th attempt returned 429 as designed.

title: Add order confirmation email infrastructure (PROPOSAL.md gap-analysis item 2)
description: Gap analysis found zero EMAIL_BACKEND configuration and zero send_mail/EmailMessage usage anywhere in the codebase - a buyer completing checkout never received any confirmation, only the /gracias/ page (lost if the tab closes). Added EMAIL_BACKEND setting (console backend default, same swappable-provider pattern as AI_PROVIDER - SMTP settings available via env vars for production, no code change needed to switch). New apps/storefront/views.py::_send_order_confirmation, called from _record_order_for_session (the single choke point for both real-webhook and fake-provider order creation) when an order is newly created and PAID with a known buyer_email; wrapped in try/except so a delivery failure never breaks the checkout flow the buyer is actively waiting on. Verified live via manage.py shell against real dev settings: the console backend actually printed a correctly-addressed confirmation email during a real checkout run, not just in the test-overridden locmem backend.

title: Password reset flow - blocked on signup not collecting email (PROPOSAL.md gap-analysis item 3)
description: Started building Django's stdlib password-reset views/URLs (same low-effort pattern SignupView already uses for UserCreationForm) but found mid-implementation that Django's PasswordResetForm looks up users by email, while SignupForm collects only username+password - would have shipped a reset flow matching zero users, existing or new. Reverted the partial build (URLs, views, one template) rather than ship something broken. Blocked on a real product decision (add email to signup - required or optional; or skip email and use a different reset mechanism entirely) - logged in FYI.md with the three concrete options, not resurrected until the user picks one.
